bugs.what: The stated goal 'reach a REAL ending within 300 turns' was not reachable for a companion-recruiting, side-quest-engaging explorer. Finishing Act 1 (Vale of Ash) fully — 3 companions, 3 verses, the crown, the Barrow Doors choice — plus light follow-on exploration consumed the entire 300-turn budget by itself. The very next quest ('The Gray') then requires resting three more of six remaining holds, or completing two full Watch services, or buying Free Company passage, just to open the road toward the next milestone (Coldpass/Marrowgate) — nowhere close to reachable in 300 turns even played efficiently.
bugs.where: overall campaign structure / status after Act I completion

bugs.what: At the Ironbound Mission, the dialogue option 'ask for the pitch' reads as an information request but actually and irreversibly resolves the 'Mission's Order' quest on the spot, committing you to the Ironbound's side of a three-way dispute (the Ironbound +1, the Gray Church -1) with no separate confirmation step.
bugs.where: Fenmarch / The Ironbound Mission / talk to Warder Iss

bugs.what: Two separately named 'drowned' locations exist with near-identical theming: 'the drowned shrine' (an Ashwood-adjacent Verses location for the Hollow King quest) and 'the drowned nave' / 'the drowned congregation' (a full, separate Fenmarch side-quest chain). Fully resolving the Fenmarch drowned-nave content (hauling and ringing the saint's bell, settling the congregation) did not advance the Three Verses tracker at all — only checking status made this clear.
bugs.where: Fenmarch: The Drowned Nave vs. Ashwood: Drowned Shrine

bugs.what: Barrow Field's room text specifically calls out 'Ivy chokes a loose-looking stone off to one side,' but no interactive action for it ever appeared in the menu on two separate visits (before and after resolving the barrow throne).

The obtained item 'the true founding record' carries the flavor hint '(read it aloud where the oath was sworn)', but no room visited in Highward (Captain-General's Hall, Parade Ground, South Gate, Record-House) offered a 'use' action for it.
bugs.where: Highward / The Record-House (item: the true founding record)

confusions: No early signal of overall campaign scale. Nothing at the outset hints that Act 1 (explicitly only one of nine holds) can absorb an entire 300-turn budget on its own if played as a thorough explorer who recruits companions and does side quests, which is exactly what the brief asked for — made it impossible to pace exploration against the 'reach a real ending' goal.

The status screen tracks two parallel 3-part verse quests with similar wording — 'Verses' (drowned shrine, old watchtower, barrow hall) for the Vale's Hollow King, and 'Old Court Verses' (the ring-ditch, the king's causeway, the mere-stone) for Barrowmere's old court — easy to conflate at a glance since both are '0/3' and both use 'verse' language.

The elder's coffer clearly gated itself in dialogue ('not open to asking... go hear what the dead king himself grieves over... then come back'), giving a concrete unlock condition. Other gated/teased content (the ivy-choked stone, the founding record's promised use-site) gave no equivalent signpost for what unlocks them, so they read as either broken or intentionally unreachable with no way to tell which.
suggestions: Give players an explicit sense of campaign scale up front (e.g., a rough turn-budget per Act, or a note that Act 1 alone is a multi-hundred-turn undertaking if explored fully) so a turn-limited playthrough can be paced sensibly.

Label irrevocable faction-commitment dialogue options for what they actually do (e.g., 'side with the Ironbound and take their pitch') instead of framing them as neutral information requests like 'ask for the pitch'.
Cross-reference or rename the two 'drowned' locations (shrine vs. nave/congregation) so their separate quest tracks are distinguishable without needing to check status.
Either add a real action for the ivy-choked stone at Barrow Field (even a flavor-only one explaining why it can't be moved yet) or drop the tease so it doesn't read as missing content.
Make a 'use <item>' action available wherever an item's flavor text promises a specific use-site (e.g. the true founding record), or name the site explicitly in the item description.
